t.7.89.2: Having dismissed all the kings, the bears, monkeys and rākṣasas, he sent away the multitude of people headed by the brāhmaṇas, filled with wealth.
t.7.89.1: Then, at the close of the sacrifice, Rāma, deeply dejected and not seeing Vaidehī, deemed this world empty. Utterly in the grip of grief, he found no peace in his mind.
t.7.89.3: Then lotus-eyed Rāma, having dismissed them all and holding Sītā in his heart, entered Ayodhyā.
t.7.89.5: For ten thousand years he performed the horse sacrifice, and likewise Vājapeya sacrifices ten times as many, rich in abundant gold.
t.7.89.6: That glorious one performed sacrifices: the Agniṣṭoma and the Atirātra, costly Gosavas, and other rites rich in sacrificial fees.
t.7.89.7: Thus that very long time would pass for the great-souled Rāghava, established in his kingdom and striving in dharma.
t.7.89.8: Bears, monkeys and rākṣasas remained obedient to Rāma's command, and kings grew more devoted to Rāghava day by day.
t.7.89.4: The delight of the Raghus chose no other wife than Sītā; and at every sacrifice, in the place of his wife, there was a golden Jānakī.
t.7.89.9: The rain-god Parjanya sends rain in due season, there is abundance of food, and the quarters are clear; the city, and likewise the countryside, is thronged with joyful and well-nourished people.
t.7.89.10: While Rāma ruled the kingdom, no one died before his time, there was then no disease among living beings, and no unrighteousness of any kind arose.
t.7.89.11: Then, after a long time, the illustrious mother of Rāma, surrounded by her sons and grandsons, met the law of time and passed away.
t.7.89.12: Sumitrā too followed her, and so did the illustrious Kaikeyī; having practised dharma in many forms, each came to dwell in heaven.
t.7.89.13: All of them were established in heaven, and those illustrious ladies, reunited with King Daśaratha, together attained the reward of their righteousness.
t.7.89.14: From time to time Rāma bestows great gifts upon brāhmaṇas and ascetics on behalf of those mothers, making no distinction among them.
t.7.89.15: Rāma, the righteous-souled, performed ancestral rites rich in many jewels and sacrifices supremely difficult to accomplish, thereby nourishing the ancestors and the gods.
